patch_description: The current SLSQP-based soft-min optimization is failing (score 0.00), likely because SLSQP struggles with the 22-variable bound-constrained problem and the log-sum-exp objective's conditioning. I replace it with a robust, fully-vectorized approach grounded in the standard technique for the Heilbronn problem: (1) analytic gradients of triangle areas in barycentric coordinates via the cross-product chain rule, (2) Adam ascent on a soft-min (log-sum-exp) lower bound of the minimum area with annealed sharpness beta, projected back onto the simplex u,v >= 0, u+v <= 1 after every step, and (3) a final "binding-constraint polish" that takes projected gradient steps using only the near-minimal (binding) triangles — exactly the active-set behavior that drives the minimum area up at the optimum. Vertices are pinned at the three corners (known to be part of good configurations) to guarantee large-scale spread. Deterministic seeds ensure reproducibility; the existing try/except fallback is preserved.
